reasons: The full text is pinned and hash-verified in a community mirror.

The paper itself is not served from an official paper-display page, so the level is B rather than A.

page_evidence.observation: The abstract connects road travel time, kernel density estimation, Rossmo's model, and two case studies.
The road metric is defined from shortest travel time with explicit street-class assumptions.
A road-metric circle illustrates how travel-time geometry differs from Euclidean distance.
A crime series is overlaid on a road-aware hotspot surface.
A three-dimensional residence-probability surface accompanies model extensions.
Computational efficiency, tests, and the conclusion delimit the model's use.
An executive summary translates both prediction outputs into investigative guidance.

abstract_structure.observation: Name the two prediction tasks, road metric, KDE and Rossmo components, and the historical case studies.

model_chain.observation: Compute shortest travel-time distance over a road graph.
Apply kernel density estimation under the road metric.
Adapt Rossmo's geographic-profiling model to road travel time.
Apply both methods to the Yorkshire Ripper and Atlanta Child Murderer data.

validation_chain.observation: Overlay known crimes and predicted hotspots for a documented series.
Discuss scalability and a limited computational test set.
Distinguish predicting future crimes from locating a residence and state investigative limits.

figures.lesson: Make the non-Euclidean neighborhood visually intuitive.
Overlay evidence points, routes, and risk surface in one spatial frame.
Separate the residence prediction from the crime hotspot map.

code_links.note: No independently packaged source tree was paired with this exact PDF; embedded appendix fragments are not treated as reproducible code.

transferable_rules.rule: When replacing Euclidean distance, visualize the induced geometry before using it in a model.
Overlay historical events on the predicted spatial field for case-level validation.
Separate two prediction targets and their permitted decision uses in the conclusion.

risks.risk: The evaluation uses a limited number of historical cases and lacks a modern out-of-sample benchmark.
Rainbow heatmaps are not perceptually uniform and can distort magnitude.
The 3D surface makes precise spatial comparison harder than a calibrated contour map.

provenance.review_method: full-page render overview plus 4-7 high-resolution evidence-page visual checks and extracted-text review
